about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: Florida Department of Environmental Protection (Algal Bloom Sampling)
channels.note: Algal bloom sampling dashboard layer; read by the fl-dep-habs feed. Blooms, not sewage. (research/fl/report.md §2.5)

channels.name: Florida Department of Environmental Protection
channels.legal_basis: Fla. Stat. 403.077(3)(b): DEP keeps an electronic mailing list with regional lists by county or district and sends each notice to it
channels.note: County e-mail subscriptions to PNP notices; the same notices as the PNP site, read through the fl-dep-pnp feed. Sign-up status: not attempted. Covers every operator in the state. (research/fl/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Florida Department of Environmental Protection
channels.legal_basis: Fla. Stat. 403.077(2)(a) and (3)(a): the owner or operator gives DEP a notice within 24 hours of discovering a release reportable to the State Watch Office; DEP publishes every notice on a public website within 24 hours of receipt
channels.note: Public Notice of Pollution (PNP): the statutory posting for every operator in the state (no CSOs in Florida). Read through the feature service by the fl-dep-pnp feed; the HTML list is https://prodenv.dep.state.fl.us/DepPNP/reports/viewIncidentDetails. Covers every operator in the state. (research/fl/report.md §2.1, §2.2)

channels.agency: Florida Department of Health county offices
channels.name: Florida Department of Health county offices
channels.note: Varies by town (county by county): county health departments issue no-contact advisories after some sewage spills, at their discretion, as news releases on each county's floridahealth.gov site; no statewide list or feed was found and the county pages are not surveyed yet. (research/fl/report.md §2.5)

channels.name: Florida Department of Health (Florida Healthy Beaches Program)
channels.legal_basis: Fla. Stat. 514.023(3)-(4): the Department of Health may issue health advisories when beach waters fail its bacteriological standards, and then notifies the city or county and DEP, which investigates wastewater facilities within one mile
channels.note: Beach sampling results and advisory flags per sampling point (beach-detail pages backed by a Caspio data page), read by the fl-doh-beaches feed. (research/fl/report.md §2.5)

channels.name: JEA (Jacksonville)
channels.note: JEA's Environmental Incident Reporting page: this month's sanitary sewer overflows (address, date and time, estimated gallons, action, whether waterways were impacted), including spills below the State Watch Office threshold. Voluntary page; fetched 2026-11-04. Snapshot only for now (records false): the lines are not yet parsed into records. (research/fl/report.md §2.3)

channels.name: Sarasota County
channels.note: Sarasota County's AbnormalEventSpill layer: sanitary sewer overflows in the county reported to DEP by the North Port, Sarasota and Venice utilities, the Englewood district, Sarasota County Utilities and private systems (date, type, gallons, whether surface water was affected, a point). Its description calls it an archive of the 2016-2020 spills, updated annually. Voluntary: a county publication no law requires. The layer's description answered 200 to the project user agent on 2026-11-04 (last edit 2026-08-17). Only the description is read (its last-edit time shows a change): the rows carry street addresses and free-text notes, and the PNP feed (fl-dep-pnp) carries the same reportable events. (research/fl/report.md, fl-sarasota-abnormal-event)

channels.name: Swim Drink Fish
channels.note: Swim Guide listings for Florida. Voluntary republisher of local beach results; affiliates not resolved. The site answered 200 to the project user agent on 2026-11-04 but shows its listings in a script app with no API: not read. The Department of Health's beach results are read as a feed (fl-doh-beaches).
channels.barrier_review: an app only (Swim Guide): no web page of its own, but no login wall either

channels.name: WWALS Watershed Coalition
channels.note: WWALS Watershed Coalition (Suwannee Riverkeeper): its Florida spills page, which links to DEP's map of Public Notices of Pollution, and its posts tagged Notice of Pollution (one post, a High Springs sewage spill of 2023-03-30, on 2026-11-04). Voluntary: a watershed group's posts. Both answered 200 to the project user agent on 2026-11-04. Read for the channel's health; not used for records: the PNP feed (fl-dep-pnp) carries the notices. (research/fl/report.md, fl-wwals)
